title: Tomato Juice with Added Ingredients, From Concentrate, Shelf Stable

content.title: About
content.content: Tomato juice is made from tomato concentrate to which additional ingredients (such as carrot, celery, spices) are added. The juice is pasteurized and sealed in airtight packaging, making it shelf‑stable without refrigeration.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Using concentrate reduces transport volume by up to 80 %.
Added vegetables increase the levels of vitamins A and C.
Tomato juice is a common base for sauces, soups, and cocktails.
In many countries it is considered a classic spring beverage.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may lower the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene and vitamin A contribute to good vision.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Tomato juice provides few calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Composed mainly of water, it helps maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or added vegetables.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain varieties contain added salt; people with hypertension should check the label.

items.title: Sugar and sweeteners
items.content: Some products add sugar or artificial sweeteners, which may be unsuitable for diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled, use it as a base for cocktails, smoothies, soups, sauces, and marinades. Fresh herbs or spices can be added to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if the package is bulged or the juice has an off‑odor.
